name: Face with Open Eyes and Hand Over Mouth
baseMeaning: A face with wide open eyes and a hand covering the mouth in shock or embarrassment.
tldr: 🫢 is a gasp for “no way,” disbelief, or amazement, and it can look surprisingly like 🤭 in a fast chat.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🫢 directly shows genuine shock at something sudden, startling, or completely unexpected.
contextMeanings.example: i cannot believe what just happened 🫢

contextMeanings.meaning: 🫢 works as a quick “no way” reaction to news, a reveal, or an impressive outcome.
🫢 can exaggerate a reaction that the sender is performing rather than genuinely feeling.
contextMeanings.example: i'm fully invested in this mess 🫢

contextMeanings.meaning: In a romantic conversation, 🫢 can express admiration for someone impressive or charming.
contextMeanings.example: okay that outfit was actually unreal 🫢

platformNotes.note: On TikTok, 🫢 often becomes part of a performed reaction to a wild reveal, dramatic post, or surprising caption. It can mark the moment a creator has caught everyone’s attention.
On Instagram, 🫢 often appears beneath a surprising photo or dramatic caption. It may express sincere amazement, though it can also be part of the post’s exaggerated reaction.
In Slack, a lone 🫢 can replace “wait, what” when a client announcement or project update comes out of nowhere. It suits ordinary disbelief, not bad news about a person.
In iMessage, 🫢 reads as a quick personal gasp, especially in a close conversation where both people already know the context. If an older device displays 🤭 instead, add a word to prevent confusion.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z users often use 🫢 as a performed reaction in short-form video comments. The exaggerated surprise is part of the joke, even when the sender is not actually speechless.
Millennials are likely to notice 🫢’s wide eyes and treat it as the cleaner, more precise gasp emoji. In ordinary messages, it often means straightforward disbelief.
Some Gen X users may first see the hand-over-mouth shape and think 🤭. Older devices that substitute 🤭 can make this confusion more frequent.

warnings.title: Mistaken for a giggle
warnings.description: “You are so funny 🫢” can arrive as disbelief when the sender meant bashful laughter. Use 🤭 for a giggle or add words when the distinction matters.

warnings.title: Loud reaction to someone’s pain
warnings.description: Replying 🫢 to a real loss or painful update can feel like reacting to someone’s pain at volume. Send ❤️, 😢, or a caring sentence instead.

seoTitle: 🫢 Face with Open Eyes and Hand Over Mouth Emoji Meaning
seoDescription: What does 🫢 mean? It is a gasp for shock, disbelief, or amazement, often used like “no way” and easily confused with the bashful giggle 🤭.

longForm.overview:
🫢 entered the emoji set in Unicode 14 in 2021, after 🤭 had already been doing the hand-over-mouth job for several years. Its original artwork was literal and precise: round, wide-open eyes and a hand clamped over the mouth. That combination looked like a gasp, so the earliest straightforward use was “I am stunned” or “no way.” It was not designed as a general embarrassment symbol.

As it spread through short-video captions, comments, and fast group chats, 🫢 became a standard reaction to something surprising, impressive, or impossible to ignore. It can report disbelief in a work channel, show admiration in a dating thread, or perform the “I’m watching and cannot look away” reaction. The crucial detail is the eyes. 🤭 has curved, smiling eyes and means a giggle or bashful “oops”; 🫢 has round, open eyes and means a gasp. On small screens those faces are easy to confuse, but they are opposites: one conceals laughter, while the other catches a shock in the act.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🫢 most often appears after a reveal: “they won the role 🫢,” “the client said what 🫢,” or a link to a post the sender cannot stop watching. A lone emoji can replace a sentence—“I did not expect this”—especially when the message is already reacting to something startling.

It also appears where the surprise is affectionate. In dating chats, “you didn’t 🫢” can mean that someone is impressive or charming, not alarmed. In comments and captions, it often functions as a performed reaction: the sender is visibly taken aback and wants the reader to share that energy. The same symbol can therefore sit inside serious conversation, although its volume makes it a poor fit for actual pain.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not send 🫢 to someone who has just reported a loss, injury, or other painful news. Its gasp is loud by design, so the message can feel like you are reacting to their pain at volume. Use ❤️, 😢, or a plain sentence instead.

Also check the eyes when choosing between 🫢 and 🤭. “You are so funny 🫢” may be meant as a bashful giggle but arrive as disbelief. If older devices render the symbol as 🤭, add words so the recipient knows which reaction you intended. In a work channel, 🫢 is fine for ordinary disbelief, but not when the subject deserves a restrained response.
longForm.howToReply:
Reply with 🫢 when you are equally surprised; the matching faces make a compact acknowledgment without explanation. For a bigger reveal, move to 😱😨 or 🤯👀. If the conversation has reached the point where the content feels genuinely overwhelming, 😱💀 can take the shock further.

If someone sends 🫢 about your post, read the context before celebrating. It may be straightforward amazement, but in a dating thread it can be admiration. If it seems to have landed on the wrong note, ask what they meant or clarify your own. If someone sent 🫢 when 🤭 would have fit, a warm 🤭👀 can playfully correct the choice without turning the moment into an explanation.

faqs.question: What does 🫢 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 🫢 usually means “no way,” shock, or amazement. It can also express admiration when the context is complimentary or romantic.

faqs.question: What does 🫢 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: The sender’s gender does not determine the meaning. Depending on the conversation, 🫢 may show surprise, disbelief, or admiration, so the surrounding message matters more than who sent it.

faqs.question: Is 🫢 flirty?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. In a dating thread, it can say that someone was impressive or charming, while elsewhere it usually means surprise without romantic intent.

faqs.question: What does 🫢 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🫢 is often a performed “no way” reaction to a surprising video or reveal. The sender may be emphasizing that they are watching and cannot look away.

conversationExamples.message: wait they actually gave her the job 🫢
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is straightforward shock at good news. Match it with 🫢 or celebrate the result with her.

conversationExamples.message: okay you actually look amazing in that photo 🫢
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji turns the compliment into an admiring gasp. Reply warmly rather than treating it as disbelief.

conversationExamples.message: the client just changed the launch date 🫢
conversationExamples.interpretation: This reports disbelief about an unexpected work development. Acknowledge the disruption and discuss next steps.

conversationExamples.message: dad sold his old truck at auction for way more than expected 🫢
conversationExamples.interpretation: The reaction is astonished amusement at a family surprise. Respond with excitement or ask for the final price.

conversationExamples.message: this plot twist actually broke me 🫢
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is performing a dramatic reaction for the audience. Match the energy or quote the detail that shocked them.
